checkstyle-needs-execution-id.problem: Running ./mvnw checkstyle:check reports hundreds of violations that the normal build never mentions.
checkstyle-needs-execution-id.solution: Invoke the project's execution by id: ./mvnw checkstyle:check@nohttp-checkstyle-validation (or @quality-checkstyle-validation).
checkstyle-needs-execution-id.title: Bare checkstyle:check runs the DEFAULT ruleset
checkstyle-needs-execution-id.why: A CLI invocation uses default-cli configuration, not the <execution> config in the pom. It falls back to Sun conventions — 413 violations here, none of them real.

clock-dependent-tests.problem: A test computing 'today' or 'tomorrow' against code that calls LocalDate.now() can fail if the clock rolls over mid-run.
clock-dependent-tests.solution: Accept it for a small validator; inject a Clock only when the ripple is worth it. Either way, flag it in the PR rather than leaving it silent.
clock-dependent-tests.title: LocalDate.now() in production code makes tests midnight-flaky
clock-dependent-tests.why: Injecting Clock into PetValidator means changing PetController, which constructs it with new PetValidator(). That exceeds a 'change PetValidator only' constraint. A known, stated limitation beats an unrequested refactor.

docker-tests-must-be-opt-in.problem: ./mvnw verify fails on a fresh clone with 'docker compose up' errors, on a machine where Docker is fine.
docker-tests-must-be-opt-in.solution: Exclude *IntegrationTests from the default surefire run; restore them with -Pcontainers, which CI uses.
docker-tests-must-be-opt-in.title: Container-backed tests must be opt-in, not default
docker-tests-must-be-opt-in.why: Compose cannot bind a port another container already holds — an unrelated postgres on 5432 breaks the build. A takeaway repo must go green without Docker, or the first thing a new clone does is fail for reasons unrelated to the change.

form-validation-lives-in-validator.problem: Adding a rule to a form and reaching for a jakarta.validation annotation on the entity.
form-validation-lives-in-validator.solution: Put form rules in the slice's Validator (e.g. PetValidator). Leave the entity's annotations alone.
form-validation-lives-in-validator.title: Form validation goes in a Validator, not on the entity
form-validation-lives-in-validator.why: Entities are shared with non-form paths (imports, fixtures, integration tests). An annotation added for a form rejects data on every path, including ones that legitimately carry historical values.

inclusive-date-boundary.problem: A date rule says "must not be in the future" and the boundary is ambiguous: is today allowed?
inclusive-date-boundary.solution: Default to inclusive — today valid, tomorrow invalid — and use isAfter(LocalDate.now()). Say so explicitly in the ticket.
inclusive-date-boundary.title: "Not in the future" means today is valid
inclusive-date-boundary.why: isAfter gives the inclusive boundary directly. isBefore/isEqual chains get this wrong under mutation testing: a survivor on the conditional means the test only checked 'some past date' and 'some future date', never the boundary itself.

mutation-survivor-means-no-assertion.problem: Coverage is high, the mutation gate fails, and it is unclear what to add.
mutation-survivor-means-no-assertion.solution: Run .claude/tools/mutation_survivors.py. For each survivor, assert the behaviour the mutation changed — do not add more tests that merely call the method.
mutation-survivor-means-no-assertion.title: A surviving mutant means the test ran the code without checking it
mutation-survivor-means-no-assertion.why: Coverage proves a line executed; mutation proves someone would notice if it changed. Adding tests without assertions raises coverage and leaves the mutation score exactly where it was.

pit-needs-1-19-on-jdk-21.problem: ./mvnw -Pmutation verify dies with 'Coverage generator Minion exited abnormally due to UNKNOWN_ERROR'.
pit-needs-1-19-on-jdk-21.title: PIT crashes on JDK 21 below version 1.19
pit-needs-1-19-on-jdk-21.why: PIT 1.17 predates proper JDK 21 support. The toolchain here reports java.version 17 but actually runs Adoptium 21, so the mismatch is easy to miss.

spring-error-codes-are-expanded.problem: A test asserts a field error code equals the one passed to errors.rejectValue(...), and fails with a longer, unfamiliar code.
spring-error-codes-are-expanded.solution: Assert that FieldError.getCodes() CONTAINS your code. Do not assert getCode() equals it.
spring-error-codes-are-expanded.title: Spring expands rejectValue codes — assert contains, not equals
spring-error-codes-are-expanded.why: DefaultMessageCodesResolver expands one code into an array from most to least specific. rejectValue("birthDate", "typeMismatch.birthDate", ...) makes getCode() return "typeMismatch.birthDate.pet.birthDate". The bare code is in getCodes(), never first.
